posts.headline: Draft night is finally over for One Nut Barner, and Put it in Ra's absurd 20-8 career mark with a 1.5 average finish still has zero rings to show for it — the résumé stays the loudest thing about him.
posts.detail: Two seasons, back-to-back top-two finishes, a 0.714 win pct, and still nothing but a 1.9-GPA highlight reel and a championship-shaped hole. If Cal Berkeley couldn't fix the academics, a draft board wasn't going to fix the ring drought.

posts.headline: Sasinci's World has drafted its team and Big Head still has to explain how a title banner hangs over a 13-15 career record — the excuses officially run out with the season.
posts.detail: One ring, a losing career mark, and a 5.5 average finish — Megamind's brain is apparently too big to notice the math doesn't add up. Don't be shocked if the monthly quit-threat drops before Week 1.

posts.headline: talentedtenthh's draft is in the books and the untalented tenth still owns the single worst résumé in Busters Anonymous — a 4-10 record and a dead-last 12th-place finish that no war room magic erased.
posts.detail: One season, one finish: 12th. The name was always ironic, but a full offseason and a completed draft did nothing to change the scouting report on Chauncey.

posts.headline: Thicks and the #FreeMaxx Champions have their roster locked, and a 14-14 career record with a 5.5 average finish means the ring — not the résumé — is still doing every ounce of the talking heading into title defense.
posts.detail: One title in two seasons doesn't erase a .500 career mark and a worst finish of 8th. Reigning champ or not, that pedigree needs receipts this year, not just a banner.

posts.headline: SwooshAnoosh finished the draft still holding the worst win percentage in the league, and nobody in the Titty Committee is losing sleep over the Prince of Persia suddenly seizing a throne.
posts.detail: A rookie season at 5-9 with an 11th-place finish is the entire body of work here — fresh roster cards don't rewrite a .357 win pct overnight.
